---
title: Sunset Fade
description: Brighten a light as the sun sets.
---

```{python}
#| include: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in Path.cwd().parents if (p / "great-docs.yml").exists()) / "docs"))
import _helpers as h
from ha_automations.apps import sunset_fade
S = sunset_fade.SunsetSettings
```

Brightens a light as the sun goes down, so the room is lit by the time it is dark. The light stays on for the evening.

## What happens

1. When the setting sun drops to `from_level`, the light turns on at `min_brightness`.
2. As the sun sinks, the light brightens on an ease-in curve until it reaches `max_brightness` at `to_level` (civil dusk).
3. After that the app leaves the light alone. Turn it off whenever you like.

There is no `start` trigger by default. The fade is always armed and runs every evening.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Brightness against sun elevation with the default settings. Time runs left to right as the sun sets."
h.fade_chart(S)
```

## Add it

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
h.usage_yaml(sunset_fade)
```

`light` is the only required setting.

## Settings

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
h.settings_table(S)
```

Unknown settings are an error, so a typo stops the app from loading instead of being ignored.

## Recipes

Start later and finish darker, for a room with good daylight:

```yaml
living_room_sunset:
  module: sunset_fade
  class: SunsetFade
  light: light.living_room_lamp
  from_level: 2
  to_level: -8
```

A softer evening light:

```yaml
  max_brightness: 30
```

Several lights: add one entry per light, each with its own name.

```yaml
living_room_sunset:
  module: sunset_fade
  class: SunsetFade
  light: light.living_room_lamp

hallway_sunset:
  module: sunset_fade
  class: SunsetFade
  light: light.hallway
  max_brightness: 20
```

## Test it

In Home Assistant, go to **Developer Tools > Events**, enter `<app name>_start` (for example `living_room_sunset_start`) as the event type and select **Fire event**. This updates the light now. Outside the dusk window the AppDaemon log says `outside fade, nothing to do`.

## Good to know

- The app only raises brightness. Turn the light up by hand and the fade leaves it there.
- Turning the light off by hand during the fade does not stop it. The next update turns it back on. A little past `to_level` the fade stops, and the light stays as you leave it.
- The app ignores the sun while it is rising, so a morning with the same elevations does nothing.
- Restarting AppDaemon during the fade is safe. It picks up at the next elevation update.
